report.tagline: An app where kirana stores, chemists and restaurants order stock in bulk directly from brands and wholesalers, with delivery and credit.
report.simpleSummary: A kirana shop owner normally buys stock from a local wholesaler or a company salesman who visits once a week. Udaan lets the owner order rice, oil, soap or medicines on an app, at wholesale prices, and get it delivered to the shop. It also lets good customers buy now and pay later. Udaan makes money on the gap between the price it buys at and the price it sells at, plus fees from brands. The hard part is that margins in groceries are thin, so it has lost a lot of money.

overview.whatItDoes: Udaan is a B2B (business to business) marketplace. Shops and small businesses buy goods in bulk on its app instead of from a chain of middlemen. Udaan handles delivery, payments and short-term credit.
howItWorks: A retailer downloads the app, adds GST or shop details, and sees wholesale prices for FMCG, staples, pharma, fruits and vegetables.
Udaan buys stock from brands like HUL or local manufacturers, or lists third-party sellers, and stores goods in its warehouses.
Orders are grouped by area and delivered by Udaan's trucks and vans, usually next day.
Retailers pay on delivery by cash or UPI, or use udaanCapital credit to pay in 7 to 30 days.
Udaan sells its own private label staples, which carry better margins than branded goods.
horeca360 serves hotels, restaurants and caterers with bulk supplies.
overview.valueProposition: Lower and clearer prices than local wholesalers, a wide range of goods in one app, delivery to the shop door and credit when you need it.

Avoid closing the shop to go to the mandi
Get credit to stock up before festivals

personas.name: Restaurant or caterer (horeca)

painPoints.pain: Many middlemen add cost between brand and shop.
painPoints.howSolved: Udaan buys closer to the source and sells directly, cutting layers.

painPoints.pain: Shop owners must close or leave the shop to buy stock.
painPoints.howSolved: Order on the app, delivery to the door.
udaanCapital offers short-term credit based on order history.
Thousands of products across categories in one app.
Prices are shown in the app, with schemes and offers visible.

coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Saves the shop owner time; but delivery cost is the biggest drag on profit.

userJourneys.name: First order
userJourneys.persona: Kirana owner in a tier-2 city

Enters phone number, shop name and GST or shop photo.
Checks atta, oil and soap prices against the local distributor.

Goods arrive next day; pays by UPI or cash.

userJourneys.persona: Kirana owner in a tier-2 city

Orders ₹40,000 of sweets, dry fruits and oil.

businessModel.summary: Udaan mainly buys goods and resells them, keeping the difference. It also earns from brands that pay for distribution and promotion, from its own higher-margin private labels, and from credit.

revenueStreams.detail: Buys from brands and sells to retailers; most of the ₹5,134 crore revenue is this.
Own brands of staples earn more per kilo than branded products.
Brands pay to reach small shops and to promote new products in the app.
Fees and interest share from udaanCapital loans with partner lenders.
Commission and delivery fees from third-party sellers.

businessModel.pricing: Wholesale prices shown per product in the app, with minimum order values. Not public as a list.
costDrivers: Cost of goods bought from brands (biggest by far)
Last-mile delivery to scattered small shops
Discounts and offers to win shops from local distributors
Bad loans on credit given to retailers
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a ₹10,000 kirana order of staples and FMCG, Udaan might earn a gross margin of about ₹500 to ₹800 (5 to 8%). Delivery, warehouse handling and payment costs can take ₹300 to ₹500 of that. Add discounts and a share of fixed costs, and in the past it lost money on many orders. That is why it cut cities, pushed private labels (higher margin) and bigger horeca orders. It now says its largest cities are EBITDA positive, but the company overall still lost ₹852 crore in FY26. Order-level numbers are estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Field sales agents who visit shops and help them sign up
First-order discounts and lower prices than local distributors
Credit offers that local distributors cannot match
Acquisitions like ShopKirana (2025) and Swiggy's LYNK distribution business to add retailers in new areas
whatBringsUsersBack: Credit limits that grow with good repayment
Saved order lists and reorder buttons
Private label staples at good prices
growth.moat: Udaan's moat is its supply chain: warehouses, trucks and routes in dense clusters, plus credit data on lakhs of shops. These take years and lots of money to build. But brands' own distributors and new rivals like Jumbotail and Reliance JioMart Partner can match prices, so the moat is not deep.

competitors.name: Reliance JioMart (Partner / Retail)
competitors.positioning: Reliance's B2B arm supplying kiranas with deep pockets and its own brands.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Udaan is independent and multi-brand; Reliance can sell at a loss for longer.

competitors.name: Jumbotail
competitors.positioning: B2B grocery marketplace for kiranas, also runs a franchise model.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Udaan is bigger and covers pharma and horeca; Jumbotail focuses tightly on grocery.

competitors.name: Brand distributors
competitors.positioning: Traditional distributors who supply one brand with salesmen visits.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Udaan gives many brands in one place with an app and credit.

competitors.name: Metro Cash and Carry / Walmart Best Price
competitors.positioning: Wholesale stores where shopkeepers go and buy.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Udaan delivers to the shop; cash and carry needs a trip.

competitors.name: Quick commerce (Blinkit, Zepto)
competitors.positioning: Consumer delivery that takes shoppers away from kiranas.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Indirect threat: if kiranas lose customers, they order less from Udaan.

northStar.why: A shop that orders every month trusts Udaan for its stock. That is the value: better prices, delivery and credit. Repeat orders also make delivery routes denser and cheaper.

improvementIdeas.problem: Shop owners spend time rebuilding orders each week.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Suggest a weekly basket based on past orders and season, raising order frequency and basket size.

improvementIdeas.idea: Price match promise on top 50 staples
improvementIdeas.problem: Retailers drop off when local prices beat Udaan.

improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fixed delivery days per area raise drops per route and cut cost per order.

improvementIdeas.idea: Live order tracking and missing item claims in app
improvementIdeas.problem: Complaints about missing items and late deliveries.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Order fill rate and complaint rate

improvementIdeas.problem: Shops hesitate to try unknown brands.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Small free packs with orders grow private label share and margin.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Private label share of staples sales

pmLessons: In B2B commerce with thin margins, growth can hurt you. Every extra order may lose money until delivery is dense.
Credit can win customers fast but brings risk. Track repayment as closely as sales.
Sometimes shrinking (exiting cities, cutting categories) is the right product decision to reach profit.
Own-brand products are a common way to fix margins in retail.

interviewQuestions.question: Udaan's revenue fell but losses also fell. Is that good?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain the trade-off: cutting loss-making orders and cities lowers revenue but improves contribution margin. Check retention and margin per order to judge.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you improve Udaan's unit economics?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break order economics into gross margin, delivery, discounts, credit losses. Pick levers: private labels, route density, minimum order value, fewer discounts.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to increase share of wallet with kiranas.
interviewQuestions.hint: Understand what shops still buy elsewhere and why. Add categories, reorder lists, credit tied to multi-category baskets. Measure share of shop's purchases.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Udaan expand to 10 new cities?
interviewQuestions.hint: No by default. Ask about cluster profitability, capital left, and whether dense existing cities can grow first. Suggest a test in one adjacent city.

interviewQuestions.question: Quick commerce is taking sales from kiranas. What should Udaan do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Treat it as a threat to customers. Ideas: help kiranas do local delivery, better range, supply dark stores as a new customer type.
